title: Polynomial-time unary truncated subtraction
statement: Let $f,g : \{0,1\}^* \to \mathbb{N}$ be functions such that the unary words of lengths $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are polynomial-time computable. Then the unary word of length $\max(f(x)-g(x),0)$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: The unary encoding of $f$ is polynomial-time computable
The unary encoding of $g$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: If two unary values are polynomial-time computable, then the unary word of their truncated difference is polynomial-time computable by the charged repeated-tail operation.
